name: Golfu
body:
Golfu
CR 4

This huge, brown-feathered owl is taller than a human, with massive talons and stern amber eyes.

XP 1,200
N Large magical beast
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 11, flat-footed 15 (+2 Dex, +6 natural, -1 size)
hp 42 (5d10+15)
Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 60 ft. (average)
Melee bite +8 (2d6+4), talon +8 (1d6+4)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks petrifying callback, petrifying screech

STATISTICS

Str 18, Dex 15, Con 17, Int 5, Wis 14, Cha 8
Base Atk +5; CMB +10; CMD 22
Feats Flyby Attack, Improved Initiative, Skill Focus (Stealth)
Skills Fly +4, Perception +8, Stealth +5
Languages Common (cannot speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Petrifying Callback (Su)

Once per day, if the golfu succeeds on a save against a spell or effect that targets it, as an immediate action it can utter a petrifying screech that affects only the creature that created the effect, as long as that creature is within 60 feet. It can use this ability in the same way when a creature confirms a critical hit against it.

Petrifying Screech (Su)

A golfu’s monstrous screech causes all living creatures within 30 feet to become slowed (as the spell) for 1d4 rounds (DC 15 Fort negates), as those who fail the save have their flesh and bones harden. A creature slowed by its screech that fails another save against it is paralyzed 1d4 rounds, and a creature already paralyzed that fails a third save is petrified.

Every 24 hours thereafter, a petrified creature can attempt a new saving throw to end the petrification, returning with 2d4 points of Dexterity damage, and the creature remains slowed as long until this Dexterity damage is healed. Stone to flesh or similar magic restores a petrified creature with no Dexterity damage. It cannot use its petrifying screech in consecutive rounds.

ABOUT

Rare and fearsome creatures, golfus are enormous, physically powerful birds that are feared for their ferocity as much as they are for their deadly screech. Four-legged, with a wingspan of approximately ten feet, their appearance is somewhat similar to an enormous owl. They have large, piercing eyes that are always alert, and their body is covered in dark, coarse feathers. Their sharp, curved beaks are designed for tearing flesh and cracking bones, and their powerful talons are capable of inflicting deadly wounds.

Perhaps the most feared aspect of the golfu is their ability to petrify their enemies with their screech. When attacked or threatened, they make a loud screeching sound that can turn their foes into crude granite statues. These statues appear mostly as they were in life, with a crude, rough-hewn texture, and a frozen, lifeless expression. This ability is especially potent against other flying creatures, causing their petrified form to crash to the ground, often shattering on impact.

Golfus are territorial creatures that fiercely defend their nests and their young. They build their nests in high, rocky crevices or in the tall grasses of mountainous regions. golfu eggs are large and speckled, and it takes four months for them to hatch. They have been known to attack humans and other intelligent creatures who venture too close to their nests or their young.
